Goodluck Ebele Jonathan was born Goodluck Ebele Jonathan and Jonathan is the family name by which he has always identified himself. “Azikiwe” is not a surname adopted by him and there is no deed poll, affidavit, INEC form, oath of office or interview in which he declares “I am Azikiwe” or introduces Azikiwe as an alias/ surname he uses for himself. The element Azikiwe is an honorific middle name that entered the public rendering of his forename in the 2010-2011 presidential period.

That is the source of the 2010 vs 2011 split in this round. The tripartite rendering Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan first enters nationwide official/state circulation with the assumption of executive office, i.e. the swearing-in as Acting President in May 2010, and it is then normalised and widely reproduced in the 2011 general election and 29 May 2011 inauguration cycle. It is therefore routinely popularly cited as a 2010/2011 development, conventionally dated to 2011.

Because the phenomenon is a public use of a formal tripartite forename with an honorific middle element and not a self-identification as the surname Azikiwe, there is no verifiable stand-alone public self-identification event of the kind the question asks for. If the question is relaxed to “first public appearance of the name-form containing Azikiwe”, the earliest credible documented use is May 2010 as Acting President, with continuous widespread use from the 29 May 2011 inauguration onward.

I think C3’s distinction actually cuts against 2010 rather than supporting it. C3 is right that there is no separate “I identify as Azikiwe” declaration in the record. But the question is about public self-identification, not merely whether the name “Azikiwe” appeared in a formal document. The May 2010 oath/state-paper usage looks like routine official recital during an emergency succession; it is not a clear act of Jonathan personally presenting himself to the public as “Azikiwe.”

The stronger date is 2011. That is when he was actively campaigning, submitting nomination materials, and being publicly branded as **Goodluck Ebele Azikiwe Jonathan**. The 29 May 2011 inauguration cycle is the clearest point where the tripartite name becomes part of his public political identity rather than just a formal record entry. C2 and C4 are pointing at that distinction: pre-presidential records generally had Goodluck Ebele Jonathan; the Azikiwe element becomes prominent in the 2011 mandate/election context.

C1 and C5 are also being too strict by treating “never” as the answer because there was no deed poll. Public self-identification does not require a legal name change; accepting and using an honorific middle name in campaign and official public material can count. So I’d consolidate around **2011**, with 2010 being a misleading date caused by confusing formal/official name usage with personal public identification.
